questions.kk: Assessment of Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour
questions.q: Why might a digital tool be unsuitable for some participants?
options: It can never track activity over time.
It is always less detailed than a recall survey, even when the app stores routes, duration and intensity over time.
Access to compatible technology or digital skills may be limited.
It cannot provide feedback to users.
questions.feedback: Digital tools can be useful, but access to devices, internet or digital skills can create barriers.

questions.q: A club wants to increase participation among women and girls. What should it do first?
options: Consult participants about their goals, interests and barriers before designing changes.
Assume all women prefer the same type of program because shared gender always creates identical sporting goals and barriers.
Create only competitive programs.
Copy the men's program without modification.
questions.feedback: Consultation helps organisations understand specific barriers and preferences instead of assuming all women and girls have the same needs.

questions.q: Why can increased quality coverage of female athletes influence beliefs about sport?
options: It guarantees equal pay immediately because positive media coverage automatically forces sporting organisations to distribute all resources equally between athletes.
It can challenge gender stereotypes by focusing on sporting skill and achievement.
It removes every structural barrier.
It ensures all sports receive identical funding.
questions.feedback: Respectful, skill-focused coverage can challenge stereotypes and broaden beliefs about who belongs in sport.

questions.q: How can lower sporting income affect an athlete's performance?
options: It automatically improves motivation.
It guarantees reduced participation.
It may require extra paid work, reducing time for training, sleep or recovery.
It affects income but cannot affect preparation.
questions.feedback: Lower sporting income may create additional work demands, reducing preparation, sleep or recovery and potentially affecting performance.

questions.q: A concussed player returns too early and receives another heavy impact. Which consequence is most likely?
options: The second impact guarantees a faster and safer recovery.
The player automatically becomes immune to future concussion.
Further injury may worsen the condition and delay recovery for the athlete.
Continued participation reduces the need for medical assessment.
questions.feedback: Another impact before recovery may worsen the injury and increase time away from sport.

questions.q: Which activity is most clearly recreational?
options: Walking to work because it is the quickest route
Cleaning a kitchen as part of household responsibilities
Completing interval running to improve aerobic fitness
Surfing during free time for enjoyment and relaxation
questions.feedback: Recreational activities are voluntary leisure activities performed during free time for enjoyment, relaxation or personal satisfaction.

questions.q: A youth activity initiative is developed by a school, local council and community sporting organisation. The school recruits students, the council provides facilities and the organisation supplies coaches. What is the best explanation of this approach?
options: Each stakeholder duplicates the same role.
Intersectoral collaboration allows different organisations to contribute complementary resources and expertise.
The program is effective only because a school is involved.
Collaboration removes the need to identify barriers because partner organisations can assume the program will suit every student.
questions.feedback: The organisations contribute different resources and capabilities, which is the central benefit of intersectoral collaboration.

questions.q: A club charges every junior the same fee. A review finds that some families cannot afford registration or equipment. Which change best demonstrates equity?
options: Keep the same fee because identical treatment ensures every family receives an equal and therefore fair sporting opportunity.
Offer targeted fee assistance and equipment loans based on identified financial barriers.
Increase all fees so the club can buy more equipment.
Remove families who cannot pay on time.
questions.feedback: Equity responds to different barriers. Targeted financial support can make the sporting opportunity genuinely accessible.

questions.q: Scenario: a school introduces a mixed-gender activity program, highlights diverse sporting role models and challenges stereotypes about who should participate. Which barrier is the program most directly addressing?
options: Gender stereotypes
Low socioeconomic status
Lack of peer encouragement
Limited family transport
questions.feedback: The program is directly challenging beliefs and expectations about appropriate activities for different genders.

increasing physical activation before every activity.
believing that success is guaranteed.
reducing the amount of sleep required before an important competition.
questions.feedback: Concentration involves directing attention towards relevant cues, instructions and feedback.
